sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: The suffix -ban/-ben expresses being inside a place. Use -ban after back-vowel words and -ben after front-vowel words.

items.english: He/She is in the living room.

sections.content: Hungarian vowels apparently have opinions about which suffix they’ll tolerate next to them — that’s basically what vowel harmony is. Think of -ban and -ben as two rival clubs with a strict dress code: back vowels (a, o, u) get waved through to -ban, front vowels (e, i, ö) go to -ben. Once you start noticing it, you’ll hear this sorting happening in almost every Hungarian word with an ending.
